cases.name: Shannon Melendi
cases.about: She was from Florida, and was a standout soccer team star at Southwest Miami High School, where she graduated from in 1992. "I idolized my big sister, she was my very own personal superhero, she was smart and witty and somehow always managed to get me out of trouble with our parents," sister Monique Benton said. "If only she was somehow able to get herself out of trouble on March 26th, 1994.” Melendi was attending Atlanta's Emory University and worked a part-time job at the Softball Country Club as a scorekeeper.
cases.narrative: Her body was never found. In 2006, he confessed that he kidnapped, raped and killed Shannon and burned her body. Hinton invited her to lunch after work. Melendi agreed and while en route to this lunch, Hinton faked taking a wrong turn then headed for his home in Rex, Ga. At some point, he pretended to get a cramp in his leg and asked Melendi to drive. Hinton then grabbed a hidden knife from the backseat of his car and forced Melendi to drive to his house. Hinton's wife and children were away, allowing him to tie Melendi up while he drove her car to a gas station, leaving it with the keys in the ignition. Later he would repeatedly rape Melendi, eventually strangling her to death with a necktie. Next, he set fire to Melendi in his own backyard, completely incinerating her body.
cases.disclaimer: CONVICTION

cases.name: Trinity Marie Kyles
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "She touched the lives of so many: a beloved daughter, granddaughter, niece, and cousin. Trinity was a shining, happy girl, the light of her family and the star of the hearts around her. She was joy personified.

With her bright brown eyes and her huge smile, Trinity 'Trin Trin" would light up any room with her sassy pink outfits. She spread love and laughter where ever she went.

She was the happiest when she was jamming to her favorite song: 'Usher's ABC Song' by Sesame Street. Trinity loved watching Sesame Street and PJ Mask, playing on her labeled tablet and hanging up video calls on her grandparents and other loved ones. She truly got a kick out of that!

Trinity was a little diva. She loved getting her hair done and admiring her beauty in the mirror--and it truly made her smile. She often wanted to strut her stuff at the park, take selfies with her mommy and her 'Roy Roy', her Bonus Dad, and pose for the camera showing her baby doll and pony how to do it.

Trinity had a taste for the sweeter things in life. A bowl of oatmeal for breakfast, along with a strawberry pop tart was her go to. She might have been little but her appetite was mighty.

Trinity had a adventurist spirit and showed early signs of leadership and independence. The couch was her playground. She thought it was the funniest thing to jump off the couch and run around barefoot.

In her short time on this side of God's creation, she exemplified love, laughter, bravery and joy in its purest form."
cases.narrative: She sustained a closed head injury to the back of her head and had several bruises on the cheeks with finger and fingernail impressions, a swollen eye, swollen forehead and bruises on her body.

cases.name: Breanna "Bre" Woods
cases.about:
She was the general manager at Black Coffee ATL in Atlanta, GA and was a yoga instructor, healer and writer.

The business wrote two posts about her on Facebook: 
"BC Fam, 
It is with the heaviest hearts we announce to you all that our general manager, Bre Woods, has gone to be with the ancestors. 
Bre was our light. 
A Friend. 
Consistent. 
Dedicated. 
Hardworking. 
Intelligent. 
Supportive. 
Bre WAS this business. An amazing artist, employee, and friend. She started shortly after we opened our doors, and has been an integral part of the business ever since. We are so fortunate, so blessed and forever changed to have been able to experience the magic that was Bre, and we are beyond devastated that such a brilliant woman was taken from the world so soon. We will shortly be sharing details on a candlelight vigil we are planning, and how you might be able to send gifts, donations and well wishes to the family. In the meantime we ask that you respect their privacy, and keep them lifted in prayer. 
Breanna, We Will Sorely Miss Your Physical Presence, but we promise that we will forever celebrate your life, your spirit, and your contributions to the world. 
In Love, 
Carl, Sean, Isaiah, Brandon 
Black Coffee ATL"


"Dear Bre, 
This is the hardest two days I’ve had in business so far. When I set out to open Black Coffee, my hope was that we’d have a family inside of these walls. Well, if we had that family you were the mother. The oil that kept the machine running. Beyond that, you were my friend. We talk every day, sometimes multiple times. We laughed, we cried, we argued, you rode for me and I rode for you. We shared life stories, goals and aspirations, dreams, and we were working on something big. You picking up the slack for me at Black Coffee has allowed me to go out and expand, and the plan was to have you expand right along with me. You had so much life to give, so many ideas, so much love, and to have your life taken from you in such a senseless, violent, cowardly act? I just can’t wrap my head around it. Sharing so many characteristics of my big sister, you became like a sister to me in this year and a half we’ve been working side by side. This hurts immensely. Today, we mourn you. But once the tears stop falling, I promise you with my life I’m going to honor your memory. As long as there is a Black Coffee anywhere on earth, we will tell the story of Bre. cases.name: Nateal Campbell
cases.about:
Her obituary said: "There are some people whose lives are measured not simply by the years they lived, but by the love they gave, the faith they carried, and the lives they forever changed. Nateal Campbell was one of those extraordinary people. Though our hearts are broken, we rejoice in knowing that she has exchanged the burdens of this world for everlasting peace in the presence of the Lord. Her earthly journey has ended, but her eternal life has just begun. Born on October 11, 1954, to Nathaniel and Beulah Trimble, Nateal was one of twelve children. From an early age, she learned the importance of faith, family, and love. She carried these values with her throughout her life and shared them with everyone she met. These principles shaped the woman she became and the legacy she leaves behind. Above all else, Nateal loved the Lord. Her faith in Jesus Christ was the foundation of her life and the source of her strength.

Above all else, Nateal loved the Lord. Her faith in Jesus Christ was the foundation of her life and the source of her strength. She walked by faith through every joy and every trial, trusting God completely. Her life reflected His love through kindness, compassion, generosity, forgiveness, and a servant's heart. She encouraged others, prayed faithfully for her family, and proved what it meant to live a life devoted to God. She graduated from Reuben McCall High School in Tallulah, Louisiana. She then moved to Las Vegas, Nevada, where she formed lifelong friendships and continued to develop the strength of character, compassion, and resilience that would define her life. She attended UNLV, where she met her husband, Charles Richard Campbell. She and her husband moved to Denver, where they would raise their eight children. Nateal worked in the social work field for many years. She participated in the Wellington Webb mayoral campaign right here in Denver, and she was proud to be part of the Governor's Board that made change in Colorado. Nateal was a co-founder of the CRC Foundation. She also loved to travel, and she loved to help others. Family was Nateal's greatest earthly treasure. She was a loving wife, devoted mother, proud grandmother, joyful great-grandmother, caring sister, cherished aunt, beloved cousin, and loyal friend."
